newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Union talks, gold price weigh on JCI.
newsitem.headline: Union talks, gold price weigh on JCI.

text.p: A protracted series of talks with a mining union and the sickly bullion price weighed heavily on shares in South African mining house JCI Ltd on Friday, dealers said.
The stock drifted down in thin volumes to a new year low of 35.00 rand, a loss of 250 cents.
Dealers said the stock was being hit by lengthy negotiations on a bout of compulsory redundancies at its Randfontein Estates Gold Mine Ltd.
Earlier this week JCI said it had allowed a technical advisor from the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) to complete a further report on the need to shed 4,000 jobs.
JCI has said the consultative process could not be extended indefinitely as the extra cost to the mine of 300,000 rand a day was threatening other jobs at the site.
"These talks seem to be dragging on," one dealer said.

Another factor helping the negative sentiment towards the firm was the sickly bullion price rceently which has failed to launch any form of sustained recovery and ignored the soaring prices of platinum and palladium.
Bullion fixed slightly easier in early European trade on Friday and was seen within a range of $340.50 to $343.50.

JCI on Friday renewed an earlier cautionary saying that discussions were continuing with mining-to-hotels group Lonrho Plc in respect of a merger and shareholders were advised to exercise caution in their dealings.
But dealers said the statement had had little effect on the share price.
